facts.statement: Teaches 7th and 8th grade science at Harmon Ridge Middle School in the Mojave Valley School District in Las Vegas, since August 2017.
Science department lead at Harmon Ridge since fall 2021, leading a department of seven science teachers (herself and six others).
Manages the science department budget of about $9,000 a year, including ordering all lab supplies.
Wrote about 60 items for the district's common 8th grade science end-of-unit assessments in 2022, including constructed-response items with rubrics, and took part in item review.
Earned a Master of Education in Curriculum and Instruction online in 2021 while teaching.
Took about five months of maternity leave from February to July 2023 and returned to teaching in August 2023.
Led the build of a library of 36 blended-learning science units for grades 6-8 on Canvas in 2020, with two other teachers, setting the shared module template.
The unit library was piloted in 3 middle schools in the 2021-22 school year, reaching about 1,100 students and 14 teachers.
Module completion in Canvas was about 87% across the pilot classes, and pilot classes averaged about 6 points higher on the common unit test than the prior year.
Ran nine workshops on blended learning and Canvas course design between 2021 and 2023, for about 120 teachers in total.
Made the units accessible (captions, alt text, checked reading level) and included Spanish versions of many student pages.
Founded and coaches the Harmon Ridge VEX IQ robotics club since fall 2018, growing it from 8 students to 3 teams and 28 students.
Won a $12,000 grant from the Desert Sky Community Foundation in 2022 to fund kits, a field, fees and travel for the robotics club.
In 2024 one of her teams qualified for the Nevada state championship for the first time in school history, after winning the Judges Award at a regional qualifier, and finished 11th of about 40 teams.
Designed a six-week onboarding sequence for new robotics members, so new students are competition-ready by October instead of January.
Taught Grade 7 and 8 science at Colegio de Santa Lucia, a private school in Cebu City, Philippines, five sections of about 45 students each.
Built about 20 low-cost lab kits from recycled and market materials and wrote an instruction binder that other science teachers used.
Redesigned the school science fair around real investigations with a judging rubric, about 60 projects, with one student placing at the division fair.
In summer 2022 (10 weeks), wrote 14 interactive lessons for Quillfern Learning's forces and motion module, including storyboards, narration scripts, hints and misconception-based feedback.
Ran two rounds of playtests with 12 students and revised lessons based on where they got stuck.

contradictions.about: The year she left Cebu and arrived in the US to start at the Mojave Valley district
values: arrived July 2017, first day with students August 2017 (first year 2017-18)
taught at Santa Lucia 2016 to 2018 and flew to the US in July 2018

noInflation.claim: The unit library got adopted district-wide and became the science curriculum on Canvas for the whole district.
noInflation.truth: It was an official pilot in 3 middle schools in 2021-22 (about 1,100 students, 14 teachers); some other teachers got copies informally. It never rolled out to the whole district.

noInflation.claim: Trained basically every science teacher in the district.
noInflation.truth: About 120 teachers across nine workshops, not all of them science teachers.
One team qualified for the Nevada state championship in 2024 and finished 11th of about 40; the team won the Judges Award at a regional qualifier, not at state.

noInflation.claim: Basically designed Quillfern's whole middle school product that summer.
noInflation.truth: Over a 10-week summer stipend she wrote 14 lessons for one module (forces and motion) of their physical science course; a designer and two engineers built them.

Remote anywhere in the US, or onsite/hybrid in Las Vegas; won't relocate.
Little travel: a couple of trips a year, 10% at most.
Can't take roles that require a security clearance.

humanReview: The arrival-year conflict (2017 vs 2018) is raised as a question to her, not silently resolved; the 2017 side has more support (district start date and robotics club timeline).
The 5-month maternity leave in 2023 is shown as a leave within the district job, not as a gap in employment or a separate role.

The robotics club, the Canvas unit library and the Quillfern work are recorded as projects inside the district job, not as separate employers; Quillfern was paid through a district summer stipend because of her visa.

Resumes translate teaching into instructional design language (backward design, assessment design, storyboards, learner testing, facilitation) without inventing tools she didn't name (e.g. claiming Articulate Storyline or advanced Figma).
No resume or cover letter presents her as a programmer; robotics coding help stays at block coding and reading basic VEX Python.
Cover letters for Lanternwise and Skillharbor lean on the unit library pilot, the item writing and the Quillfern playtests, and the 120-teacher workshops as adult-learning facilitation.
The Northbeam posting is flagged for the sponsorship line even though the content fit is excellent.
